purpose: Choose selectable leaf IDs from a hierarchical tree with independent expansion and derived tri-state branches.
behaviorProvider: Aegis tree model helpers and custom native ARIA tree composition.

component: Store selected leaf IDs in controlled/default state. Branch state is derived from descendants; mixed branches toggle to fully selected. Disabled ancestors/leaves do not participate in selection propagation and existing disabled selections remain unchanged.

Keep expanded IDs independent from selection; deduplicate expansion updates. Only expanded descendants enter visible navigation order. Controlled/default values are initialization/ownership boundaries, not persistence.

Provide roving focus with Up/Down, Home/End, Right expansion/child navigation, Left collapse/parent navigation, Enter/Space selection, Ctrl/Meta+A selection and * sibling expansion. Printable-key prefix search uses a 500ms buffer.

Render tree/treeitem/group roles, aria-multiselectable, checked/mixed states, expansion, level, position and set size. Decorative checkbox marks are aria-hidden; expand buttons are outside the Tab order.
When a controlled collapse removes the focused node, choose a visible enabled ancestor. Restore DOM focus only when focus fell to document.body, avoiding theft from another focused control.
host: Supply a finite acyclic tree with unique stable IDs, meaningful labels and selected leaf IDs. Own search/filter data, lazy loading, virtualization, authorization and persistence; no native form name or submission adapter is provided.

Owned styling belongs to the input token group. Actual nested shared components retain their own group and behavior; preserve four theme/mode mappings and keyboard-visible focus.

limitations: Source-backed requirements, not a current test certification or release approval.
This is custom tree behavior, not a Base UI tree primitive or an assertion of complete APG conformance.
No single-selection mode, readOnly mode, lazy fetching, drag reordering or virtualized tree is supplied.
The optional count is announced using the existing events suffix; the wrapper does not expose a localized count-label formatter.
